It affects a ring of 16 different cards and was discovered through a typology scan that matched the unusual micro-charge run signature across multiple unrelated customers.

sar.narrative: This report details suspicious online activity involving customer C12975 and their card C12975-K2. Between January 5 and January 26, 2017, the card was subjected to a series of unauthorized online micro-charges. The customer explicitly denied making the flagged transaction, prompting an investigation. The activity consists of six online charges, all under $10, occurring on six different days. The specific transactions are: ID 3660255 on 2017-01-05 for $3.51; ID 3660256 on 2017-01-07 for $5.18; ID 3660257 on 2017-01-14 for $2.66; ID 3660258 on 2017-01-18 for $4.75; ID 3660259 on 2017-01-22 for $4.99; and ID 3660260 on 2017-01-26 for $2.90. This activity is highly suspicious because the card had zero similar charges in the preceding 90 days, and the exact same micro-charge run signature was detected on 15 other cards during the same 30-day window, indicating a coordinated attack. The total exposure for this card is $23.99.
